Class ViewTUI

java.lang.Object
it.polimi.ingsw.client.ui.tui.ViewTUI
All Implemented Interfaces:
UserInterface
public class ViewTUI extends Object implements UserInterface
Text-based user interface for the Mesos game, implementing UserInterface.

ViewTUI renders the entire game state into a raw terminal using JLine 3. The screen is divided into three side-by-side panels drawn inside Unicode box characters:

  • Left panel — turn order queue, current phase, era, round, and active player (drawQueuePanel(int, int, int)).
  • Centre panel — board tiles with totem indicators, upper and lower drawable-card rows (drawCenterBoard(int, int, int)).
  • Right panel — per-player stats, discounts, and card inventories (drawPlayersPanel(int, int, int)).

Below the panels a separator line divides the game area from a scrolling log area that holds up to 8 entries. All rendering goes through a double-buffered approach (screenBuffer / colorBuffer) that is flushed atomically via flushBuffers().

Layout tiers

The layout adapts to the terminal width through the ViewTUI.LayoutTier enum: COMPACT (< 120 cols), STANDARD (120–179 cols), and LARGE (≥ 180 cols). Column proportions are recalculated on every WINCH (window-resize) signal, via handleResize(). If a full-screen overlay (help/status/end-game/ranking) is open when the resize happens, that overlay is redrawn in place instead of the main layout, so it doesn't disappear from under the player while they are still expected to dismiss it with Backspace.

Input loop

start() runs a blocking readline loop on the calling thread. Raw input is parsed by CommandParser into Command objects that are executed directly; unrecognised input is reported in the log area.

Thread safety

All methods that write to the terminal or the internal buffers are synchronized on this. Server-callback methods (e.g. onMoveUpdate(TileDTO, String), onEvent(EventDTO, List)) may be called from network threads and are safe to invoke from any thread.

    • activeOverlayRenderer

      private volatile Runnable activeOverlayRenderer
      When non-null, points to the render callback of the full-screen overlay currently being displayed (help, status, end-game, or ranking screen). While an overlay is active, a terminal resize must re-invoke its renderer instead of redrawScreen(); otherwise the resize watcher would silently replace the overlay with the main game layout, leaving it invisible while the overlay's own input loop keeps blocking on Backspace. Reset to null as soon as the overlay is dismissed.

    • initJline

      public void initJline()
      Initialises the JLine Terminal and LineReader.

      Sets up:

      • System properties to prefer Jansi over JNA for ANSI handling.
      • Alternate-screen mode (enter_ca_mode) so the game UI does not contaminate the shell scroll-back buffer.
      • An invisible cursor for cleaner rendering.
      • A WINCH signal handler that calls handleResize() whenever the terminal is resized.
      • A TUICompleter that provides context-sensitive tab completion for game commands.

      Errors during terminal construction are printed to stderr; the application can still run in degraded mode without a full terminal.

    • start

      public void start()
      Runs the main input loop: prompts for a nickname until login succeeds, then enters a blocking readline loop that parses and executes Command objects.

      The loop terminates on UserInterruptException (Ctrl-C) or EndOfFileException (Ctrl-D) by calling System.exit(int) with status 0. All other exceptions are caught and reported via log(String).

      This method blocks the calling thread indefinitely and should be invoked from the application's main thread.

      Specified by:
      start in interface UserInterface

    • computeLayout

      private boolean computeLayout()
      Reads the current terminal dimensions, selects the appropriate ViewTUI.LayoutTier, and computes all layout metrics stored in the layout* fields.

      Returns false and sets layoutValid to false if the terminal is too small to render a meaningful UI (width < 20 or height < 10). In that case callers should skip rendering.

      Returns:
      true if the layout was computed successfully; false if the terminal is too small

    • handleResize

      private void handleResize()
      Reacts to a terminal resize (from the WINCH signal handler or the polling resizeWatcher).

      If a full-screen overlay is currently being displayed (see activeOverlayRenderer), its own renderer is invoked so it adapts to the new terminal size in place. This is essential because those overlays block their owning thread inside a Backspace-only read loop and have no other way to react to a resize; without this, the previous behavior of always calling redrawScreen() would silently overwrite the overlay with the main game layout, making it look like the screen "disappeared" until the player blindly pressed Backspace to dismiss it.

      Cached terminal dimensions are refreshed unconditionally so that the polling watcher does not keep re-triggering for the same resize while an overlay (which doesn't update screenW/screenH itself) is being shown.

    • redrawScreen

      private void redrawScreen()
      Redraws the entire screen, updating all visual components and the output buffer. This method ensures proper synchronization, flushes buffers, and manages terminal display. The method performs the following tasks: - Validates terminal and reader availability; exits early if they are absent. - Pauses terminal interactions for safe rendering. - Clears the terminal buffer. - Computes and verifies the screen layout dimensions; if computation fails, resumes terminal and exits. - Initializes screen and color buffers to represent the updated terminal content. - If a model with a non-empty queue exists: - Draws layout boxes for left, center, and right panels. - Populates individual panels such as queue, center board, and player information. - If no valid model or queue exists: - Displays a default waiting message at the center of the screen. - Renders a horizontal separator line on the screen. - Iterates through logs and displays them at the appropriate positions on the screen, up to the screen's height. - Flushed the content buffers to the terminal to reflect changes. - Redisplays the prompt for user interaction. - Resumes terminal interactions. This method ensures a consistent user interface state and proper rendering of UI components, handling exceptions silently during drawing operations in case of errors in UI updates.

    • redrawQueuePanel

      private void redrawQueuePanel()
      Partially redraws only the left (queue) panel without touching the other two panels or the log area.

      Falls back to a full redrawScreen() if the cached layout is invalid, the screen buffers have not been allocated yet, or the model is not yet ready (e.g. while waiting for a reconnection to complete) — drawing a partial panel against a stale or empty model produces corrupted output instead of the "waiting" placeholder.

    • scrollPlayersPanel

      public void scrollPlayersPanel(int delta)
      Scrolls the players panel by delta rows and redraws it.

      Only the trivial < 0 case is guarded here. The upper bound (maxOffset, the number of content rows that overflow the visible panel height) depends on the wrapped card labels for every player, which can only be computed inside drawPlayersPanel(int, int, int); that method clamps playersScrollOffset against it before drawing, so scrolling past either end is a harmless no-op.

      Specified by:
      scrollPlayersPanel in interface UserInterface
      Parameters:
      delta - number of rows to scroll; positive scrolls down, negative scrolls up

    • flushBuffers

      private void flushBuffers()
      Serialises screenBuffer and colorBuffer into a single ANSI-styled string and writes it to the terminal in one pass.

      Surrogate pairs (characters outside the Basic Multilingual Plane) are handled by detecting high-surrogate / low-surrogate pairs and emitting them together with the style of the high-surrogate cell. After writing, InfoCmp.Capability.clr_eos clears any stale content below the last rendered row.

    • drawPlayersPanel

      private void drawPlayersPanel(int startRow, int startCol, int maxWidth)
      Renders the right panel: per-player nickname (colored), stats line (PP, food, stars), discount line, and the card inventory.

      Cards belonging to GROUPABLE_CHARACTERS types are collapsed into a count label (e.g. "3x GATHERER") to save space. All other character cards and all building cards are listed individually via buildCardLabel(CardDTO). Labels wrap to the next line when they exceed the available width.

      Only the rows that fall within the current vertical scroll window (driven by playersScrollOffset and scrollPlayersPanel(int)) are actually written to the screen/colour buffers; a lightweight pre-pass first computes the wrapped card labels and the total content height for every player, which lets playersScrollOffset be clamped to [0, maxOffset] before anything is drawn — so a shrinking roster or a terminal resize can never leave the view scrolled past the end of the (possibly now-shorter) content, and a single redraw with a stale offset never renders a blank panel. A small ↑/↓ indicator is drawn in the top-right/bottom-right corner of the panel when there is hidden content in that direction.

      Parameters:
      startRow - first usable row inside the panel box
      startCol - first usable column inside the panel box
      maxWidth - maximum number of columns available for text

    • printAt

      private void printAt(int row, int col, String text, int maxWidth, org.jline.utils.AttributedStyle style)
      Writes a string into the screen and color buffers at the given position, truncating to fit within maxWidth columns.

      Truncation rules:

      • If the display width of text fits within maxWidth - 1, it is written as-is.
      • If maxWidth ≤ 3, as many code points as fit are written without an ellipsis.
      • Otherwise the string is cut and "..." (3 columns) is appended.

      Wide characters (CJK, emoji, etc.) and surrogate pairs are handled correctly: a wide character is never split across a boundary.

      Parameters:
      row - target row; ignored if out of bounds
      col - starting column; ignored if out of bounds
      text - the string to write; null or empty is a no-op
      maxWidth - maximum number of terminal columns to use (including the one reserved as a guard column)
      style - the AttributedStyle applied to every cell of the output

    • reconnect

      public void reconnect(int matchId)
      Called when the client successfully reconnects to an ongoing match, restoring the board view to the current game state. Clears the log area and logs a reconnection confirmation followed by a waiting message.

      Also invalidates the cached layout so that any panel-update notification arriving from the server while waiting for the other players to reconnect (e.g. their own onCurrPlayerUpdate/ onPhaseUpdate echoes) is forced through a full redrawScreen() instead of a partial redraw. Without this, a partial redraw could run against the stale board from the pre-crash session and corrupt the display.

      Specified by:
      reconnect in interface UserInterface
      Parameters:
      matchId - the ID of the match the player reconnected to
